messages.body_plain: Hello, I’m trying to plot a barplot with two statistics to the right of my tree. When I set the position to “dodge2” to separate the bars into two, the position of the plot is to the left (and overtopping) the phylogenetic tree, and the offset to move the barplot is ignored. Any help is greatly appreciated!

messages.subject: Re: Scaling branch width by support (or other parameters)
messages.subject_clean: Scaling branch width by support (or other parameters)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

any news on this? It would be a nice feature actually resembling iTOLs functionality "Branch metadata display -> Bootstraps / metadata -> Display -> Width" (branch widths are calculated from the metadata values).

Cheers Bastian

On Monday 25 July 2022 at 16:19:04 UTC+2 kurt.wo...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hello all:
>
> I've gotten into the habit of using branch width to show clade support in my tree figures but typically do this manually. It recently occurred to me that there could be a way to do this programmatically in ggtree but I have been unable to figure it out on my own.
>
> What I want to do is specify a branch/line width using the "support" parameter of the tree as a threshold. For example, all branches with support >= 0.7 will have width = 4 while all branches with support < 0.7 have width = 2. Is this possible?
>
> Cheers,
>
> Kurt Wollenberg, Ph.D.
>
> Contractor - MSC, Inc. | A Guidehouse Company
> Phylogenetics Specialist
> Scientific Support Section

messages.subject: Problem annotating bootstrap values
messages.body_plain:
Hello everybody. I am making a phylogenetic tree but when I add the bootstrap values ​​I get some greater than 100. I leave you the code I am using:

library(ggtree)
library(viridis)
library(gdata)
library(dplyr)
library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggnewscale)
library(gplots)
library(paletteer)
library(scales)
library(ape)

arbol_seg_s <- read.tree("arbol_segmento_s_ref_SN.fa.treefile")

# Enraizar el árbol en un nodo específico (por ejemplo, en la raíz)
arbol_enraizado <- root(arbol_seg_s, outgroup = "L37904.1")

datos <- read_excel("metadata_segmento_S_sn.xlsx")

Pais <- data.frame("Pais" = factor(datos$Pais))
Año <- data.frame("Año" = factor(datos$Año))

rownames(Pais) <- datos$ID_nuevo
rownames(Año) <- datos$ID_nuevo

arbol_enraizado$tip.label <- datos$ID_nuevo

p1 <- ggtree(arbol_enraizado, layout = 'rectangular') +
    geom_tiplab(size = 2.0) +
    geom_text2(aes(subset = !isTip, label = as.numeric(node.labels)), hjust = -0.3) +

    theme(
        legend.position = "none",
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(
            size = 15,
            face = "bold",
            hjust = 0.9,
            vjust = -15
        )
    )

p1 <- p1 + theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0, "cm")) # Ajustar según necesidades

p2 <- gheatmap(p1, Pais,
               offset = 0.01,
               width = 0.20,
               color = NULL,
               colnames = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(name = "Pais",
                      values = c("chile" = alpha("#5499C7", 0.5),  # Ajustar transparencia con alpha
                                 "argentina" = alpha("#A569BD", 0.5)),  # Ajustar transparencia con alpha
                      breaks = c("chile", "argentina"),
                      labels = c("Chile", "Argentina")) +
    theme(legend.position = "right",
          legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
          legend.box = "vertical",
          legend.margin = margin()) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(keywidth = 0.7, keyheight = 0.7)) # Ajusta keywidth según tus necesidades

p3 <- p2 + new_scale_fill()

print(p3)

I would be very grateful if you could help me
